questions.q: What is the function called when money allows us to compare the worth of a shirt and a book?
questions.a: This is the "Measure of Value" function. A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing the act of buying (medium) with the act of pricing (measure).

questions.q: Why does a shopkeeper accept money for groceries instead of asking for the specific item you produce at your job?
questions.a: Because money is a "Medium of Exchange" that is universally accepted. If a student answers "because money is shiny," they are focusing on physical properties rather than the economic utility of the currency.

questions.q: If you keep 500 rupees in a savings box to buy a cricket bat next month, which function of money are you using?
questions.a: This is the "Store of Value" function. A wrong answer shows the student does not understand that money allows us to delay consumption to the future.

questions.q: How does money solve the problem of a farmer who wants to sell wheat to buy a tractor, but the tractor seller doesn't want wheat?
questions.a: Money acts as a medium of exchange; the farmer sells wheat for money, then uses that money to pay the tractor seller. If the student mentions "barter," they have missed the core point that money eliminates the need for the seller to want the buyer's specific goods.

questions.q: Is it better to store your wealth in perishable goods (like milk) or in money? Why?
questions.a: It is better to store wealth in money because money does not rot, whereas milk spoils quickly. This confirms the "Store of Value" function is essential for economic stability.

questions.q: Create a scenario where someone uses money as a "Standard of Deferred Payment."
questions.a: An example would be a student borrowing a pen from a friend and promising to pay them 10 rupees next week. A poor answer would describe a simple cash-and-carry transaction, missing the "future payment" aspect.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Money is a ______ accepted tool that functions as a medium of exchange, a measure of value, a store of wealth, and a standard for future payments, allowing people to trade easily without swapping goods directly.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you have a basket of ______, but you really want a geometry box.
What is Money? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Money is a universally accepted tool that functions as a medium of exchange, a measure of value, a store of wealth, and a standard for future payments, allowing people to trade easily without swapping goods directly.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Money?
questions.a: Students often think money has value because of the paper it is printed on.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify which function of money is being used in specific real-world scenarios and explain why a barter system fails in those same situations.
